sections.history: Tiruchittremam, at Sitthaimur near Aalathampadi, between Thiruvarur and Thiruthuraipoondi, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned in the Tevaram by Appar and Sundarar, and reckoned the 106th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. (Sources differ on district: Wikipedia places it in Tiruvarur, the TN Temples Project in Nagapattinam.)
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Ponvaithanathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Akhilandeswari in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram keep the form of the Shiva temples of the lower Tiruvarur delta.
sections.legends: The name Ponvaithanathar, 'the lord who set down gold,' comes from the sthala legend: in the absence of a devotee named Sankaran, the lord provided for his wife, leaving a gold coin for her each day at nearby Ponnirai — pon-vaitha-nathar. Shiva is worshipped here with the goddess Akhilandeswari, 'mistress of all the worlds.' As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Thiruvarur–Thiruthuraipoondi stretch of the Paadal Petra trail include Tiruchittremam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruchittremam the pilgrim comes to the lord who set down gold. Before Ponvaithanathar and Akhilandeswari, in the lower Tiruvarur delta, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple, and the memory of the lord's daily gift to a devotee's household.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruchittremam is at Sitthaimur, near Aalathampadi between Thiruvarur and Thiruthuraipoondi, in the Tiruvarur delta. Thiruvarur and Thiruthuraipoondi are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
